Subject: BlueWave evaluation plan & technical rollcall — proposed timeline

Dave — great to meet last week. To keep momentum toward your Q3 launch target, I wanted to introduce the Redwood technical team and propose a short mutual action plan that covers the evaluation checkpoints we discussed. Goal here is to align stakeholders, confirm success criteria, and lock a tight evaluation/close timeline so your internal teams can plan.

High-level ask: please confirm who from BlueWave will be the primary engineering point-of-contact (we used Dave for now) and whether Sophie will be involved for product/PO decisioning. Once confirmed, Soojin and Karthik will run a focused SE/ML kickoff and hand off a runnable eval plan.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): Technical kickoff (SE + ML) — define perf targets and dataset scope
- Week 1: Eval run #1 (latency/cost smoke test) with 1k sample requests
- Week 2: Deep eval (quality regressions, edge cases) + regression monitoring hooks
- Week 3: Final report + commercial term review
- Week 4: Decision & next steps (PO signoff / Dedicated capacity scoping)

Attachments: BlueWave_MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP draft) and redwood_eval_plan_template.xlsx (eval checklist & data schema).

Soojin will lead the SE kickoff and run the perf baseline; Karthik will outline ML-specific success criteria (model variants, tokenization, KV cache behavior). Marissa will coordinate logistics and procurement touches.

Next steps: can you confirm the engineering lead(s) and availability for a 45-minute technical kickoff next week? Suggested slots: Tue 4/26 10–11am PT or Wed 4/27 2–3pm PT.

Thanks — Ben

--

- Provide expected max sequence length and typical batch shape (avg tokens per request and concurrency). This informs kernel selection and batching ops from our runtime.

Attachments referenced: redwood_eval_plan_template.xlsx (uploaded as XLSX and Google Sheet).

Shared Drive (editable): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xQ-BlueWave-MAP

Hi all — quick ML-engineering notes to make the kickoff productive. A few specifics we will want to lock during the SE session:

1) Model variants and quality gates
- We’ll propose 2 model families: a high-throughput quantized variant (low cost) and a high-quality FP16 variant for edge-case tests. Define explicit acceptance criteria (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE thresholds, hallucination rate on a labeled subset).

2) Tokenization & preprocessing
- Confirm tokenizers, any domain-specific token additions, and normalization rules. Differences here change token counts and cost estimates.

3) KV cache behavior and session anchoring
- If you plan multi-turn flows, share expected session lengths and whether you want persistent KV caches for active users. This impacts memory and throughput planning.

4) Sample payload sizes and concurrency
- Please provide 3 representative payloads and a target concurrency profile (p50/p95 requests per second) for the first-run.

5) Observability hooks
- We’ll drop a lightweight tracing hook and token-level cost telemetry into your sandbox for the deep eval; we need confirm on log access (S3 bucket or VPC tunnel).

I’ll prepare a short checklist doc for the kickoff and a minimal script to run the week-1 smoke tests.

Cheers — Karthik
